summary.intent: Close a race in `addrConn` connection establishment (grpc/grpc-go#7365): hold `ac.mu` continuously from the idle-state check in `connect()`/`updateAddrs()` through `resetTransportAndUnlock()` setting `Connecting`, so two overlapping callers can no longer both start a transport for the same `addrConn` and leak an orphaned connection.
summary.issue_fit: Met — the described race window (two `tryAllAddrs` invocations racing past the idle check) is closed by construction; the regression test `Test/AuthorityRevive` that exposed it passes at head (single run, race-detector clean). The PR's specific claim of zero flakes over 100000 attempts is not independently reproduced given this run's five-minute focused-test bound, but the closed race window (confirmed by verification) makes repeating that measurement immaterial to the decision.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff reviewed (clientconn.go, the only changed file, +6/-7 across 3 hunks). Traced `connect()`, `updateAddrs()`, `resetTransportAndUnlock()`, and the `updateAddrs()` -> `GracefulClose()` -> `onClose()` interaction across base and head. Ran `go build .`, the full root-package test suite, a race-detector run of the three unit tests closest to the changed paths (`BackoffCancel`, `ResetConnectBackoff`, `UpdateAddresses_NoopIfCalledWithSameAddresses`), and a race-detector run of `Test/AuthorityRevive` itself, all at head 76ef33f4 — all pass. Three concurrency safety premises verified by an independent fresh-context worker, all `holds`.

observations.fact: The deferred `ac.transport.GracefulClose()` in `updateAddrs()` (clientconn.go:986) now runs while `ac.mu` is still logically held (ownership transferred to the goroutine spawned at clientconn.go:996), so its synchronous `onClose` callback (clientconn.go:1351-1353) can briefly block on `ac.mu.Lock()` until that goroutine reaches its own unlock — a latency change from the prior code, not a deadlock (confirmed by verified premise-3).

requirements.evidence: clientconn.go:905-923 (connect) and clientconn.go:940-996 (updateAddrs) hold `ac.mu` from entry through the call into `resetTransportAndUnlock` (clientconn.go:1234), which itself never re-locks at entry; verified concurrency-safe (premise-2 holds).

requirements.source: spec-pr7390/body/"This ensures that no concurrent requests are able to start once caller of resetTransport does some validation and calls resetTransport"
requirements.evidence: Independent verifier ruled premise-2 `holds`: `ac.state` cannot leave `Idle` without `ac.mu` held continuously through the `Connecting` transition, so two concurrent `connect()`/`updateAddrs()` calls cannot both pass the idle check.

requirements.source: spec-pr7390/body/"Verified that Test/AuthorityRevive no longer flakes for 100000 attempts with the change"
requirements.evidence: Reran `Test/AuthorityRevive` once with `-race` at head 76ef33f4: pass. Repeating 100000 iterations exceeds this run's five-minute focused-test bound, so the exact flake-rate claim is unrepeated; nothing material depends on it since the code-level trace and verified premise-2 independently establish the race window is closed by construction.

requirements.source: spec-pr7390/release-notes/"client: fix race that could lead to orphaned connections and associated resources"
requirements.evidence: Matches the closed race: before this change `updateAddrs()` could start a second `tryAllAddrs` while a first was still in flight, and only one resulting transport was ever assigned to `ac.transport`/closed, per arjan-bal's 2024-07-09T06:38:44Z comment. No externally observable contract changes, so Released compatibility does not apply.

Root cause (addrConn.connect() releasing ac.mu before resetTransport() re-acquired it, per arjan-bal's 2024-07-04T07:02:02Z root-cause comment) is eliminated: verified premise-1 and premise-2 both `holds`.

tasks.premise: Every code path through `resetTransportAndUnlock` (clientconn.go:1234-1304) unlocks `ac.mu` exactly once before returning, given the function's contract that the caller already holds `ac.mu` on entry and never locks it itself.

`ac.state` only transitions away from `connectivity.Idle` while `ac.mu` is continuously held from the moment `connect()` (clientconn.go:905-923) or `updateAddrs()` (clientconn.go:940-996) observes the prior state, through the point `resetTransportAndUnlock` sets `connectivity.Connecting`, so two concurrent calls into `connect()`/`updateAddrs()` cannot both observe `Idle` and both proceed to start a connection attempt.

Handing off a locked `ac.mu` from `updateAddrs()`'s goroutine to a newly spawned goroutine running `resetTransportAndUnlock` (clientconn.go:996, `go ac.resetTransportAndUnlock()`) is safe in Go because `sync.Mutex` is not goroutine-owned, and no code path requires the spawning goroutine to reacquire or rely on `ac.mu` being unlocked before the spawned goroutine runs, including the `defer ac.transport.GracefulClose()` at clientconn.go:986 (whose synchronous `onClose` callback at clientconn.go:1351-1353 also tries `ac.mu.Lock()`), which merely blocks until the spawned goroutine unlocks rather than deadlocking.
